beginner.stem: How many protons does a Yttrium atom have? (That number is also its place on the table.)
beginner.explanation: Yttrium is element 39. A neutral atom has 39 protons and 39 electrons.

beginner.stem: Compare catalog first ionization energy: Yttrium vs Rhodium. Which is larger?

beginner.stem: Compare catalog melting point: Yttrium vs Rhodium. Which is larger?

beginner.stem: What boiling point does this catalog list for Yttrium?

beginner.stem: Compare catalog boiling point: Yttrium vs Rhodium. Which is larger?

beginner.stem: Compare catalog density: Yttrium vs Rhodium. Which is larger?

beginner.stem: Which of these is a listed use of Yttrium?

beginner.stem: Which history line belongs to Yttrium?
options: William Hyde Wollaston, working in secret on platinum residues, isolated rhodium in 1803.
Element 99 was found in the debris of the Ivy Mike thermonuclear test of 1952.
Axel Fredrik Cronstedt isolated a metal from the ore Kupfernickel, devil’s copper, in 1751, and named it nickel.
Johan Gadolin examined a black mineral from Ytterby, Sweden, in 1794 and separated a new earth, yttria.

beginner.stem: How does the catalog describe the discovery of Yttrium?

Johan Gadolin dissolved a black mineral from the Ytterby quarry, later called gadolinite, in acid.

beginner.stem: Which story title belongs to Yttrium in this catalog?

beginner.stem: Which story title belongs to Yttrium in this catalog?

beginner.stem: Which story title belongs to Yttrium in this catalog?

beginner.stem: Which story title belongs to Yttrium in this catalog?
beginner.explanation: A ceramic of yttrium, barium, and copper carried electricity with no resistance at a temperature that liquid nitrogen could reach.

beginner.stem: One listed emission line of Yttrium is near which wavelength?
beginner.explanation: The catalog lists a Yttrium line at 404.76 nm (violet).
